question.text: Godavari Opportunities AIF (Cat II, closed-ended). Called-up Capital INR 80 crore, Hurdle Rate 9% (compounded annually), fund has completed 3 full years with NAV tracked on a 'reference hurdle NAV' basis (starting at committed capital). What is the Reference Hurdle NAV at the end of Year 3?

explanation.text: The Logic: In a closed-ended Cat I/II fund, Hurdle NAV COMPOUNDS year over year. Year 3 Hurdle NAV = INR 80 crore x (1.09)^3 = INR 80 x 1.295029 = INR 103.60 crore (rounded to INR 103.59 crore), matching keyed option B. Workbook p.119 is explicit that the hurdle is a compound rate, not a simple rate. The Trap: A is simple interest: INR 80 x (1 + 3 x 0.09) = INR 101.60 crore; C and D are mis-compounded (wrong rate or periodicity). Note: Closed-ended Cat I/II hurdle NAV compounds annually off committed capital — Hurdle NAV at Year N = Committed × (1 + hurdle)^N. Simple-interest variants are typical distractors.
